transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just finished your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or how you're getting on with your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora, thanks for checking in. I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. So you should be fine to get back to it soon if it's been a week or more.

Just avoid any heavy lifting or strenuous work for about a month after your operation.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for that information. My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using it now, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you're not sure or need more of it, your GP should be able to provide some for you.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That sounds good, thank you. I'm also very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.text:
It's common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How long has it been since your operation? If your vision is still quite blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, I think that covers everything. Thank you for your help, Dora!
